name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,359

clue.text: Appeal in religious foundation is top concern

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it is placed inside that word's letters

blocks.note: a priory is a monastery or convent founded under a prior
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A monastery's governors worry chiefly about attracting visitors or donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' reads as a fundraising plea, but it is the sense of allure, which slang calls 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever matters most and must be dealt with first is the thing given precedence over everything else.

clue.text: Notice small truck

blocks.note: first meaning: to detect or become aware of, as a verb
second meaning: a light open-backed vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase is a verb in one sense and a noun in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up on something is to notice it, and a pick-up is a light van with an open load bed.

clue.text: Priest heading off with American, tragically flawed figure

indicators.note: with its heading taken off the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a vicar is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman leaves with an American, a figure of tragic flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' sounds like the priest leaving; it removes his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the boy who flew too near the sun on wax wings fell to his death through overreaching pride.

clue.text: Edition in series on poet largely superfluous

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside its letters
largely means for the most part, so all but the last letter is used

blocks.note: a run is a series, as of performances

explanation.surface: Another edition in a series on a poet is mostly unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer needed or more than required is surplus, which is the sense of superfluous.

clue.text: Something prickly in old snooker star, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the name is wanted for its sound not its spelling

blocks.note: Willie Thorne, English snooker player and commentator

explanation.surface: Something spiky is found in a former snooker champion, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Willie Thorne was a well-known English snooker player of the 1980s; snooker is a cue game like pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp spine on a plant stem is a classic example of a prickly thing.

clue.text: Wicket taken by bowler, say, with one following? A hypothetical scenario

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
a bowler is one kind of hat, the 'say' marking it as an example
f. is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator imagines a wicket falling to a bowler, followed by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' tempts as the cricketer, but it is the hat; a bowler hat is a rounded felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an imagined possibility, and is used as a noun for any speculative 'suppose this happened' situation.

clue.text: Language retained by church in difficulty

indicators.note: what is retained is held within, so the answer is kept inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the next two

explanation.surface: A church struggling financially keeps up a particular tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a major Indo-Aryan tongue spoken across northern India and is one of that country's official languages.

clue.text: Support before seen to be held by Irish politician wobbled

indicators.note: something held by another is clasped inside it

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a TD (Teachta Dála) is a member of the Irish parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Before an Irish politician got support he looked unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: TD is the Irish equivalent of MP, a member of the Dáil.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to sway unsteadily as if about to fall, the same motion as wobbling.

clue.text: Disrespectfully light-hearted element in family - it's less familiar

blocks.note: one's mother's or father's side of the family

explanation.surface: A cheeky, irreverent member of the family is regarded as less familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less familiar' looks like describing that relative, but it defines the B-side of a record, the less well-known face.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of a single or of a situation is the side people know less well, like a record's B-side.

clue.text: Clubs close to fans in modern curved road

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken
one element in another goes inside its letters

explanation.surface: Clubs near their supporters sit on a curving modern street.
explanation.definitionFit: A street built in an arc, typically lined with terraced houses, is named after the shape of a new moon.

clue.text: Dispelling of ridicule on air about a foreign manager

indicators.note: dispelling scatters things, so the letters of the phrase are dispersed and regrouped
about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the following word

explanation.surface: Mockery broadcast on radio about an overseas football boss finally stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudio Ranieri is the Italian football manager who famously won the Premier League with Leicester City in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an Italian who has managed many clubs, including Chelsea and Leicester, so to English readers a foreign manager.

clue.text: See 10
Vessel carrying you on the Seine in reversal of direction

indicators.note: a vessel carrying something holds it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel
tu is French for you, the Seine placing us in France

explanation.surface: A boat on the Seine taking you aboard has to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'the Seine' suggest a boat on the river; the vessel is a pot, and the river only signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning right round to go back the way one came is the manoeuvre named after the shape of the letter.

clue.text: Northern idiot entertaining rogue in set showing spite

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone within, so the second element sits inside the first
rogue means wayward and out of control, so the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: A northern fool welcomes a scoundrel into his circle and behaves spitefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a person being entertained, but it is an adjective telling you to rearrange 'in set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malicious ill-feeling, and nastiness is the quality of being mean and unkind to others.

clue.text: Comedian has life reformed in consequence after bother

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged
one element placed in another goes inside its letters

blocks.note: to harry is to harass or pester
an end can be a result or outcome

explanation.surface: A comic changes his ways after getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the trouble word first. Harry Enfield is a British comedian known for TV sketch shows.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a well-known English comic performer, so he is an instance of the general term for a funny entertainer.

clue.text: Feature of tennis or another sport?

blocks.note: first meaning: exchanging shots back and forth over the net
second meaning: motor racing over public or off-road stages

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the first sense is a gerund describing an activity in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Long exchanges of shots are called rallies in tennis, and motor rallies are a separate motorsport discipline.

clue.text: Self-employed person concerned with style in football club bottom of league

indicators.note: these elements placed in another go inside its letters
the bottom of a down word is its final letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in names like Fulham FC

explanation.surface: A contractor cares about style at a football club languishing at the foot of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who sells services to several clients rather than holding one job is self-employed.

clue.text: Lone trip devised for anti-crime organisation

indicators.note: something devised is worked out and put together anew, so the letters are reconstructed

explanation.surface: A solo journey is planned for a police agency.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the international body that coordinates police forces across countries to fight cross-border crime.

clue.text: Peers say invested in a Greek publishing company

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so the short word goes inside

explanation.surface: Lords put money into a Greek publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' suggests members of the House of Lords; here it means people of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: One's peers are contemporaries of similar age or standing, the people forming one's own cohort.

clue.text: Outfit for retirement?

blocks.note: surface reading: what one wears after leaving work for good, a pensioner's wardrobe
setter's reading: retiring for the night, going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement suggests ending a career, but to retire is also simply to go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightgowns are the garments people change into when they go to bed at the end of the day.

clue.text: Ill-will shown in country clique lacking heart

indicators.note: without its heart the word loses its central letters

explanation.surface: A heartless national faction displays hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-will is the wish to harm others, which is exactly what malice is.

clue.text: Cheerful relative between start and end of journey

indicators.note: something between two others is flanked by them
only the first and final letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A relative is in good spirits throughout a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty manner is lively and self-confident, showing a breezy good mood.

clue.text: A joy almost certainly found in journalist that's discerning

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
things found in something lie inside it, so the run of letters goes inside the last element

blocks.note: ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A writer's undeniable delight shows real discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost certainly' reads as one phrase meaning probably, but 'almost' trims 'certainly' alone: YES becomes YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with the sharp sight of a bird of prey notices fine details, which is what being perceptive and discriminating means.

clue.text: Show excessive feeling in demo televised

indicators.note: the answer sits in the following words, lying across their join

explanation.surface: Protesters overact when their demonstration is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion theatrically, especially in an exaggerated way.

clue.text: Object having bird in drive

indicators.note: one word in another goes inside its letters

blocks.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for drive

explanation.surface: Someone protests at finding a bird on the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to voice doubts or reluctance, which means raising an objection to something.

clue.text: Eastern monk mentioned animal

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so we want the word as it sounds rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A Himalayan monk talks about a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid kept for wool and as a pack beast is a kind of mammal.

clue.text: Female musician cutting quiet single? It could be her

indicators.note: something cutting into another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a single in cricket is one run
Yoko Ono, the artist and singer

explanation.surface: A woman musician gets onto a quiet record and is identified as the star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' reads as a record, but it is a cricket single, one run. 'It' and 'her' are themselves examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as 'it' and 'her' stand in place of nouns, so either word is an example of this part of speech.

clue.text: One on board is back working in large house

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the short word is read from its end

blocks.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
on means operating, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A company director returns to work at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship or a company board; here it is a game board.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a big, imposing residence, so the two words together name it plainly.

clue.text: US city models, withholding nothing, in slips

indicators.note: withholding means keeping back, so the round letter for nothing is kept out of the word

blocks.note: models poses as an artist's sitter does

explanation.surface: Los Angeles fashion models hold nothing back in their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' tempts as petticoats; it is the definition in the sense of errors or lapses of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake or failure of concentration, just as a lapse is a momentary error.

clue.text: Novelist rarely discontented in feature of countryside

indicators.note: without contents the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An unhappy writer seldom ventures out into the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' reads as unhappy but means 'with the contents removed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Green foliage and plants make up much of what one sees in rural landscapes, so this vegetation is typical of it.
